levels.title: Design Your Agent
levels.desc: One mission, five questions. Nothing here is templated for a specific use case — every field maps directly onto a real Lyzr agent.

missions.title: Mission 1 — Design your agent
missions.desc: There's no 'right' answer to any of these — this is your agent, doing your job, in your words.

missions.codeTemplate:
from lyzr_adk import Studio

studio = Studio(api_key=API_KEY)

agent = studio.create_agent(
    name={{agent_name|tojson}},
    provider={{model|tojson}},
    role={{role|tojson}},
    goal={{goal|tojson}},
    instructions={{instructions|tojson}}
)

assist.tradeoffs: There's no wrong shape here — but a narrow, specific role produces more predictable behavior than a broad one. If you're unsure, write the role as if you were assigning this exact job to a new hire on day one.
assist.mistakes: The most common mistake at this step: writing 'goal' as a personality trait ('be helpful and friendly') instead of an outcome ('resolve billing questions without escalating to a human'). Lyzr uses goal to steer behavior and tool-use decisions, not tone.
assist.docs: See Lyzr Quickstart: Option D — every field here maps 1:1 onto the real POST /v3/agent payload (name, provider, role, goal, instructions).

finalize.testMessage: Hi — introduce yourself and tell me what you can help with.
